# gilguard

> Raise a detailed error the moment an import re-enables the GIL on free-threaded Python.

## Docs

### API Reference

#### When the GIL comes back on
> What gilguard raises or warns with, and the report that comes with it.

- [GILEnabledError](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/GILEnabledError.html): The GIL was enabled on a free-threaded interpreter
- [GILReport](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/GILReport.html): Everything gilguard knows about why the GIL is on
- [GILGuardWarning](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/GILGuardWarning.html): Emitted instead of raising when the action is `warn`

#### Turning the guard on and off
> `import gilguard` calls install() for you. Use these to choose the action in code or to stop guarding.

- [install](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/install.html): Start guarding imports
- [uninstall](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/uninstall.html): Stop guarding imports

#### Checking the interpreter
> Small helpers you can use with or without the guard installed.

- [is_free_threaded_build](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/is_free_threaded_build.html): Check whether this interpreter is a free-threaded build
- [gil_enabled](https://mkennedy.codes/docs/gilguard/reference/gil_enabled.html): Check whether the GIL is enabled in this process right now
